summary: Compose Telegram text publishing through the provider-neutral Social Core API and crash-safe worker runtime.

impacts.evidence: Channels, publications, leases and receipts use explicit organization/workspace scope and FORCE RLS.
Publication text is tenant content; events and receipts exclude bodies, tokens and provider error payloads.
Five additive authenticated Social API operations are generated into all public SDKs.
Existing Social Core v1 events are reused without payload changes.
The existing additive SocialPublisher SDK-v1 interface is composed unchanged.
Migration 17 adds append-only receipts and extends the existing worker lease kind.
Bot tokens remain callback-scoped; host egress is fixed HTTPS/public-address/redirect-deny and raw provider responses are not logged.
Only admitted account/channel text writes execute; destructive edit/delete stay disabled.
Every canonical transition remains atomic with audit/outbox; remote identity is append-only operational evidence.
Receipt-aware recovery finalizes confirmed writes and fails unknown outcomes without duplicate sends.
Fixed Telegram Bot API egress is added; inbound webhooks remain excluded.
Worker emits bounded component/deferred events and publication status exposes normalized failure codes.
Binary rollback preserves canonical publications and receipts; remote messages are not destructively reverted.
Registry, API, worker recovery, migration, contract, SDK and frontend gates cover the new runtime.
